components.note: Tail definition identical to the source; empty-family convention and E(Z;A) notation stated; the small-event notion is the source's epsilon-delta property made uniform. Restricting the definition to integrable families loses no uniformly integrable family, since the source's own remark makes every such family integrable.

source_evidence.item: Exercise 4.6.1 hypotheses and conclusion: i.i.d. Z_i with E|Z_i| finite, independent theta with finite mean, Y_i = Z_i + theta, E(theta|Y_1..Y_n) -> theta a.s.
Exercise 4.6.1 statistical reading with the bold-face terms prior distribution and posterior distribution

components.gap: Supply the statistical reading of Durrett's Exercise 4.6.1 (p. 248): with normal(0,1) noise the observations are a sample from a normal population with variance 1 and unknown mean; the law of theta is the prior distribution, and the conditional law P(theta in . | Y_1, ..., Y_n) is the posterior distribution after n observations, so the theorem concerns the posterior mean. The entry now uses 'integrable prior variable' and 'posterior consistency' without these definitions or that reading.
components.note: Hypotheses, the normal case and the a.s. and L1 conclusion are proved (strong law, measurable version of theta, upward theorem); only the source's definitions and statistical interpretation are missing.
